questions.prompt: If you are under 18, what is the youngest age at which you may apply for an instruction permit?
questions.explanation: Minors must be at least 15½ years old to apply for an instruction permit, and at least 16 to get a license.

questions.prompt: As a minor, what must you complete before you can get an instruction permit?
questions.explanation: Minors must complete driver education to get a permit. The 50 hours of practice and the drive test come later, before the license.

questions.prompt: To get a Class C instruction permit, which tests must you pass?
choices: The knowledge test, and no others.
questions.explanation: You must pass the knowledge test and a vision test to get a permit. The drive test comes later, for your license.

questions.prompt: Your parents share joint custody of you. Who must sign your permit application?
choices: The parent you live with most.
questions.explanation: If parents or guardians share joint custody, both must sign the application.

questions.prompt: By signing a minor's permit application, what does the parent or guardian accept?
choices: A duty to ride along on every single drive.
The cost of driver training lessons.
questions.explanation: A parent or guardian signing the application approves it and accepts financial responsibility for the minor.

questions.prompt: You are 15½ and just got your instruction permit. When may you start using it?
choices: Right away, with any licensed adult.
Once your driver education class ends.
questions.explanation: Minors may not use a permit until they start behind-the-wheel training with an instructor, who validates it.

questions.prompt: As a minor with an instruction permit, who may supervise your practice driving?
choices: Any adult 21 or older, licensed or not.
questions.explanation: Minors with a permit must practice with a California-licensed driver at least 25 years old.

questions.prompt: You are 20 and have an instruction permit. What is the youngest the licensed driver with you may be?
questions.explanation: Adults with a permit must drive with a California-licensed driver at least 18. The 25-year minimum applies to minors.

questions.prompt: Where must the licensed driver supervising a permit holder sit?
choices: Anywhere in the car, front or back.
In the back seat, to watch the road.
questions.explanation: The supervising driver must sit close enough to take control of the vehicle if needed.

questions.prompt: If you are under 18, what is the youngest age at which you may get a driver's license?
questions.explanation: Minors must be at least 16 to get a driver's license.

questions.prompt: As a minor, what is the shortest time you must have held your instruction permit before scheduling the drive test?
questions.explanation: Minors must hold a permit for at least 6 months, or turn 18, before scheduling the behind-the-wheel test.

questions.prompt: What is the least supervised practice a minor must complete before getting a license?
questions.explanation: Minors must practice at least 50 hours with a California-licensed driver 25 or older, including 10 hours at night.

questions.prompt: Of a minor's 50 required practice hours, what is the least that must be at night?
questions.explanation: At least 10 of the 50 practice hours must be driven at night.

questions.prompt: As a minor, what must you prove to get your driver's license?
choices: Driver education, but not driver training.
Driver training and your own insurance policy.
questions.explanation: Minors must prove they completed both driver education and driver training.

questions.prompt: As a provisional driver, how long are you barred from driving between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m.?
questions.explanation: Provisional drivers can't drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. during their first 12 months with a license, unless an exception applies.

questions.prompt: You are 17 with a provisional license. May you drive your 19-year-old friend to the mall?
choices: Yes, since your friend is over 18.
Yes, as long as it is during the day.
Only with a parent or a driver 25+ along.
questions.explanation: Provisional drivers can't carry passengers under 20 unless a parent or guardian, or another licensed driver at least 25, is with them.

questions.prompt: In your first year with a provisional license, you must drive home from work after 11 p.m. What must you carry?
choices: A note signed by your parent.
Nothing; work trips are always allowed.
A note signed by your employer.
questions.explanation: To be excused for work, a provisional driver must carry a note signed by the employer confirming the job.

questions.prompt: To drive for a school activity under the exception, a provisional driver needs a note signed by:
choices: A DMV examiner at your local office.
questions.explanation: For schooling or a school activity, carry a note signed by the school principal, dean or designee.

questions.prompt: A provisional driver must drive for a medical need with no other way to travel. What must they carry?
choices: A note signed by a parent.
Nothing, if the need is truly urgent.
A note signed by a physician.
questions.explanation: For a medical need, carry a physician-signed note giving the condition and the expected recovery date.

questions.prompt: To drive an immediate family member under the exception, a provisional driver needs a note signed by:
questions.explanation: To drive an immediate family member, carry a note signed by a parent or legal guardian stating the reason, the family member, and when the need ends.

questions.prompt: Can a parent or guardian cancel their teen's driver's license?
choices: Yes, by filing a cancellation form.
No, only the DMV can cancel a license.
Only after the teen gets a ticket.
questions.explanation: A parent or guardian may cancel a teen's license by completing a Request for Cancellation or Surrender of a Driver License or ID Card.
